- If sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30-day horizon; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If 18-day history shows strong upward trend, model tends to overreact; apply mean reversion bias: subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast if price > 72.00.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00) and history shows low volatility, model overfits noise; use 3-day moving average of past 30d to anchor forecast.
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum (e.g., >+1.5% per day), model lags; add 0.3–0.7% lag correction to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- For 30d forecasts, if model’s first 5 days are >72.00, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence bias.
